_comment: Sensors with no machine-readable feed. Updated by research, not by fetch.py. Each carries its own 'asof' date; the dashboard marks anything older than 45 days as stale so a forgotten sensor cannot quietly pass for a current reading. state: 0 calm, 1 watch, 2 turning.

A4.detail: The Q2 2026 calls in late July went the other way. Jassy: Amazon 'will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026', and expects the same in 2027; Alphabet also described itself as supply-constrained; Microsoft's Hood said that outside the useful-life change 'our calendar year 2026 CapEx investment expectations remain unchanged' while Nadella brought 31 new data centres online in the quarter. All four raised guidance: Amazon to about $220bn, Alphabet to $195-205bn, Meta's floor to $130-145bn. Amazon's 'disciplined ROIC framework' is exactly the false positive this sensor's note warns about — discipline said to investors alongside a raise, not instead of one.
A4.source: Q2 2026 earnings calls (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta), late July 2026

B2.detail: CBRE puts primary-market vacancy at 1.4%, down from 1.6% a year earlier; JLL has North America at about 1%. Both are record lows. H1 2026 absorption was 25 GW, double the year-earlier half. Preleasing rose to 80.4% of all capacity under construction from 74.3%, and under 1,500 MW of future capacity is available across all primary markets — roughly six months of demand at the current rate.
B2.source: CBRE North America Data Center Trends H1 2026; JLL midyear 2026

B3.detail: The August reading — construction falling for the first time since 2020 — has been overtaken. Capacity under construction across the US primary markets rose 24.8% in H1 2026 to a record 7,481 MW, past the old 6,350 MW peak. The watch stands on the other half of the sensor: cancellations are clustering, not isolated. Twenty US projects were killed in Q1 2026 alone after 25 in all of 2025 and 6 in 2024, and Data Center Watch counts $130bn of projects blocked or delayed by community opposition in Q1 2026 — about as much in one quarter as in all of 2025. Rule 05 applies with full force: the stated reasons are power, transformers, permits and local opposition, which is the opposite of demand failing.
B3.source: CBRE H1 2026 pipeline data; Data Center Watch (June 2026); cancellation reporting

C1.value: ~$220bn issued by August, ~40% of the buildout debt-funded
C1.detail: Hyperscalers issued roughly $121bn of bonds in 2025, more than four times the five-year average; by 2026-08-10 the same group had issued about $220bn, and AI accounts for roughly 30% of net US investment-grade issuance. Off the balance sheet: Meta's Beignet joint venture raised $27bn, and Blue Owl and JPMorgan put about $13bn into the SPV owning Oracle's OpenAI site at Abilene. Microsoft added a quieter version in July — extending building useful lives moves future data-centre leases from finance to operating leases, cutting reported 2026 capex from about $190bn to $175bn with the economic plan unchanged; the commitment leaves the capex line without leaving the company. Still short of the turn: Morgan Stanley's split of the ~$2.9tn to 2028 is about $800bn private credit, $200bn bonds and $150bn securitised — near 40%, not most.
C1.source: BIS Quarterly Review (March 2026); Morgan Stanley buildout financing estimates; Microsoft FY2026 Q4 disclosure

C3.value: 5-6 years for servers, Microsoft stretches buildings 15 to 25
C3.detail: Microsoft extends the useful life of data centres and office buildings from 15 to 25 years with FY2027, on 'our operating history and expected use of these assets'. On servers the group still points in two directions: Amazon shortened a subset from six years to five citing the pace of AI development, booking $920m of accelerated depreciation and a $700m hit to operating income, while Meta extended to 5.5 years and took $2.9bn less depreciation. Critics put $176bn of understated depreciation across 2026-2028 if economic life is nearer three years. The turn is a shortening across the group or a write-down; one filer moving alone is not it.
C3.source: 10-K and 10-Q useful-life disclosures; Microsoft FY2026 Q4 call; depreciation debate coverage

C4.value: record $510bn in H1, structures still clean
C4.detail: Global venture funding hit a record $510bn in H1 2026, more than the $440bn of all 2025, and AI took over 70% of Q2 dollars. OpenAI and Anthropic alone account for $217bn, 43% of the half. The half splits $305bn in Q1 and $205bn in Q2 — a sequential fall, but off a concentration spike rather than a broad retreat, and the turn needs two consecutive falling quarters. Q3 closes on 2026-09-30 and is the first real test. No reporting yet of ratchets, preference stacks or compute credits substituting for cash.
C4.source: Crunchbase Q2 and H1 2026 global funding data

D1.value: PCs -4.9%, phones -6.7%, one quarter short of the turn
D1.detail: Both device markets are now falling in units. PCs shipped 68.2m in Q2 2026, down 4.9% year on year — the first decline after nine quarters of growth. Smartphones fell 6.7% to 277.5m, the second consecutive year-on-year decline after -4.1% in Q1. Revenue keeps rising as memory costs are passed through: memory is up nearly 300% year on year and is over 65% of the bill of materials at the low end, and IDC does not expect the shortage to ease before early 2028. IDC's full-year 2026 smartphone forecast has been cut from -13.9% to -16.7%. The threshold is more than 5% down for two quarters running: phones cleared 5% only in Q2, PCs only once. One more quarter at this pace turns this sensor.
D1.source: IDC quarterly shipment trackers, Q1 and Q2 2026

D4.value: budgets still expanding, renewal cliff ahead
D4.detail: No reported cancellation wave at the large sellers, and the budget direction is still up: 86% of enterprises plan to raise AI budgets in 2026 against about 2% planning a cut, roughly 40% by 10% or more, after enterprise generative-AI spending tripled from $11.5bn in 2024 to $37bn in 2025. The counterweight is that only 5-8% report measurable at-scale ROI, and Gartner frames 2026 as the year the 2025 contracts come up for renewal and have to justify themselves. That is a forecast, not an observation — and per the sensor's own note, qualitative evidence scores watch at most.
D4.source: Forrester and Gartner 2026 enterprise AI outlooks; vendor results
